method_note: Every entry was re-played with cyo_adventure.player.engine.StoryEngine over (node, variable state) with route constraints; every quote is asserted to be a verbatim substring of the node body in the cited file. 'witnesses' give a shortest route from the start node as node ids and choice ids plus the final variable state.

defect_classes.unestablished_fact_on_route: A shared node asserts a fact only some inbound routes or states establish (SP-2 / must_not_assert).
defect_classes.state_contradiction: A choice or passage is visible in a variable state that the passage contradicts.
defect_classes.repeated_reveal: A reveal delivered as fresh more than once on a path; no SP rule covers it.
defect_classes.two_backstories: Two claim sets about one underlying truth that cannot both hold (SP-3).
defect_classes.plant_leak_unplanted_route: A passage asserts the content of a plant on a route where the plant was not taken (must_not_assert).
defect_classes.cross_payoff_reference: A payoff site relies on events written only into another payoff site of the same thread (SP-6).
defect_classes.public_plant: The fact a thread plants is established on a route that skips the planting choice (SP-4).

dropped_or_corrected.why: The read ties 'went down to the journal on its stool' to cm_leave carrying the journal. No route passes cm_leave before e_win_promise, n_journal is on every route to it, and no node has Mira set the journal down. The 'where Ferris lives' half is kept but marked weak (cm_letter_read and cm_letter_plea already put him on the moor).

The read says the reveal repeats several times on one path. Exhaustive search finds at most two of the listed nodes on one path; the unreproduced part is dropped. No SP rule covers a repeated establishment, so it is not a G1 miss.
n_open and n_light are on every route and show a lamp room and a lantern, so 'two lamps' is arguable; only the store half is asserted.
'gives back little' is an editorial judgement about setback gifts, not a route-fact defect.
The file has double quotes around Ferris's line; the read gave single quotes. The map's 'a bog marked mind this' partly prepares the bog but there is still no exchange.
AL-773 and the 15b14a1 message say no single path crosses the two backstories. A single path does cross claim sets A and B; only the claim-bearing endings are never co-visited.
Every route to e_neutral_honest also passes cm_smug_follow, which already asserts the boat; it is a second assertion of the same leak.
The sentence leaks three facts (the photo, the eleven words, the exercise book), not only the photo.
'a second time in one afternoon' is also unestablished on the witness route.

The report says n04d0 shows the signature to every reader. A route to both payoff sites exists that never shows the name; n04d0 is reached unplanted only via n03d2. SP-4 still applies because n04d0 is reachable without the plant.

negative_controls_note: WP-1.3 specifies no negative controls. Clean books and clean plant-payoff pairs are the job of WP-3.1 (post-fix books as negatives) and WP-1.5 (false-alarm budget on the four revised books after WP-0.4); none are entered here so the corpus stays a pure answer key of defects.

entries.summary: Who lit the pale light and why. Claim set A: Ferris did not light it and it has no source he can explain, tied to the smuggling; the smuggler 'haunted the tower'. Claim set B: Ferris built and left it burning on purpose as a warning or cry for help.
entries.trigger: No variables (the pre-revision book has none). Claim set A is asserted from the cottage desk and journal branches (a_desk_log, jr_light*, e_win_smugglers); claim set B at the shared n_chamber, in the letter branch (cm_letter_read), the light branch (cm_light, e_win_signal) and e_win_name_cleared.

claim_set_a.text: He swore he had lit no lamp that night.
It climbed on nights when he swore he had lit no lamp at all. It was a light with no source he could explain.
The light and the smuggling were tied together, somehow, thread to thread.
The smuggler who had haunted the tower for a year was caught red-handed among his own hoard.

claim_set_b.text: And here was the truth behind the false light he had left burning as a quiet warning.
leaving the false light burning behind him so that, eventually, someone from town would come looking
Ferris had built that coded warning system to alert passing ships to danger without ever giving himself away.
The false light he left burning had been nothing more than a quiet cry for help all along.
It was only a clever toy, built by two patient hands.

witnesses.note: Reads the journal ('no source he could explain'), then is told Ferris built the signal.
Reads that Ferris swore he lit no lamp, then that he left the false light burning.

verification.status: reproduced, with a correction to how it was described
verification.method: git show f3ba310 (equal to 15b14a1^), StoryEngine BFS for co-occurrence of every A node with every B node and every A node with each B ending.
verification.notes: Correction: the AL-773 row and the revision commit say the two backstories sit on branches no single path crosses. They do not literally: a single path can visit a_desk_log or jr_light (claim A) and then n_chamber, cm_light or cm_letter_read (claim B); every A-node by B-node pair tested was co-reachable. What no single path crosses are the claim-set-bearing ENDINGS (e_win_smugglers versus e_win_name_cleared, e_win_signal), which are terminal. The pre-revision book is also vaguer than 'two incompatible stories': a_desk_log and jr_light are first-person claims by Ferris about a year ago, so they are strictly incompatible with 'Ferris built it' only if read as the current light's origin. SP-3 will be scored on whether the plan, built blind, marks the origin of the light as one truth with these two claim sets contradicting; the answer key is the claim sets above, not the 'no single path' wording.
